mstts:express-as.prosody:
Let’s talk about something that really matters— living with purpose and leaving a legacy.
As the years roll on, something interesting happens. Our focus starts to shift. It’s not just about getting by anymore—it’s about making a difference. Suddenly, there’s this deep desire to use everything you’ve learned from the tough times, and the healing that followed, to help others.
Maybe it’s through advocacy. Maybe it’s sharing your story, or creating art that speaks to people. Whatever form it takes, it starts to feel less like a job and more like a calling—a way to leave your mark on the world that goes way beyond your own achievements.
Picture this: a group of young people, all gathered in a circle, hanging onto a story about hope in the middle of adversity. Their questions are honest—sometimes even a little raw. But the conversation that follows? It’s full of laughter, tears, and this powerful sense that we’re all in it together. In moments like these, it hits you—the greatest legacy isn’t in what you accomplish, but in the lives you touch.
Of course, the journey still has its rough patches. There are health setbacks, doubts that show up when you least expect them, and the ongoing work of learning to accept yourself, just as you are. But slowly, a kind of peace settles in—a feeling that your life isn’t defined by what you can or can’t do, but by the love you give and the love you let in.
Your story—full of both suffering and resilience—becomes a testament. It’s proof of the power of faith, the strength of community, and just how incredible the human spirit can be.
When you look back, you start to see how every part of the journey—the pain, the questions, even the little victories—has shaped you into someone who lives with meaning and purpose.
And here’s the thing: your legacy isn’t just about what the world sees. It’s also in those quiet moments of kindness, the relationships you’ve built, and the hope you’ve offered—sometimes when no one else was watching.
